name: South Dakota

law.summary: No statute or rule found that requires public notice of a sewage overflow. Permittees report overflows to DANR (24 hours oral, 5 days written under standard permit conditions) and, since the eRule, file the written report through EPA's NeT-SewerOverflow, which makes South Dakota one of the few states whose overflow reports are public in EPA's daily extract. The general spill rule (ARSD 74:34:01) covers regulated substances, not sewage.

barriers.what: No public notice duty and no operator web notices found; SOBE is the only public trace
SOBE rows are 5-day written reports, so events surface days to weeks late
barriers.note: A 24-hour public posting would need a state or operator channel.

readiness.rationale: EPA's daily SOBE extract carries event-level SD reports with start, end, coordinates and volume; the ingester exists. Delay is the 5-day written report path.

owner_questions: Accept SOBE (5-day reports, median 5 days late) as South Dakota's event feed and label it 'Dated reports, delayed'?
Show basement backups and on-plant spills with no receiving water, or only events that reached water?
surprise: South Dakota, with no public-notice law and two tiny CSO towns, has one of the best event feeds in the country because its small-town permittees file every overflow through EPA's NeT tool: 207 events with coordinates.
